subject: Capacity tiling & prompt/response profile for Centurion pilot
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@centurionai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity tiling & prompt/response profile for Centurion pilot

Hi Liam,

Great to meet last week — excited about Centurion's pilot scope. To get our Dedicated capacity recommendation aligned with your expected user experience, can you fill out the short profile below and attach a representative CSV or a small sample of session traces? Key things we need up-front:

- Expected concurrent active sessions (peak and typical).
- Prompt length distributions (percentiles for user prompts and system prompts).
- Average and 95th-percentile response lengths (tokens).
- Percent of requests that need streaming vs single-shot.
- Typical request rate per user (requests/day) and burst windows (duration + multiplier).
- Any strict latency SLOs per route (p50/p95/p99).

If it's easier, a 24–72 hour trace sample from your staging logs works fine; column names like session_id, ts, prompt_tokens, response_tokens, route are enough. I've attached a lightweight template (centurion_session_sample.csv) — fill what you can and we'll run a quick tiling simulation.

Next steps: once we get the sample, Marissa will run a preflight that includes tiling suggestions (GPU mix, oversubscription margins, kv-cache sizing) and we'll propose a pilot committed capacity with canary routing. Goal: a recommendation and cost/latency tradeoffs in 3 business days after we have the sample.

Thanks — kim

--
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0122

Attachment: centurion_session_sample.csv (CSV template, 3 KB)
From: Liam O'Connor <liam@centurionai.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 Jul 2028 13:04:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Capacity tiling & prompt/response profile for Centurion pilot

Kim — thanks, attaching a short extract from our staging logs. A few clarifications inline: 

- Peak concurrent active sessions: ~1,800 (observed during internal load tests), typical daily peak is ~900.
- Prompt lengths: median 32 tokens, 75th 68 tokens, 95th 210 tokens. We have a small tail to ~1,200 tokens for long context queries.
- Response lengths: median 120 tokens, p95 ~1,100 tokens (rare).
- Streaming: ~22% of requests use streaming (progressive content generation).
- Request rate per user: average 14 requests/day, but power users spike to 80/day.
- Burst windows: 6–12 minutes during feature drops, with a ~3x multiplier on baseline QPS.
- Latency SLO: target p95 < 400 ms for lite routes; p95 < 1.2s acceptable for long-form generation.

Two asks from our side: 1) can you confirm whether KV cache persistence across sessions is feasible in Dedicated for our use case? 2) we use a mix of open models and proprietary fine-tuned checkpoints — can you recommend an approach to pin/checkpoint variants for rollouts?

Liam
Ops Lead, Centurion AI
liam@centurionai.com

Attachment: centurion_trace_sample_excerpt.csv (5 KB)

Subject: Re: Capacity tiling & prompt/response profile for Centurion pilot

Thanks for the sample, Liam — useful distribution. A few quick technical notes and assumptions I'll run in the preflight: 

- Long-tail prompts (~1,200 tokens) and p95 responses ~1,100 tokens push memory usage and KV cache retention. We'll simulate with a hybrid tiling: some M60-style reserved slices for heavy sessions and smaller dense slices for high-concurrency short prompts.
- Streaming needs continuous KV write/read patterns; we'll assume streaming sessions hold KV for session duration (configure retention policy === 5–10 minutes after last request by default).
- For pinning model variants: recommend using model-version routing with canary slices (10% of traffic) + automatic rollback on latency/quality regressions. We can host both open and proprietary checkpoints in the same Dedicated pool if the customer provides the artifacts and a signed EULA for on-prem/runtime usage.

Preflight I'm planning:
1) Run token-cost simulation across 24h with three tiling candidates (1x high-memory, 2x mixed-density, 3x oversubscribed cheap).
2) Estimate GPU-hours, expected p95 latency envelope per route, and projected unit cost/token.
3) Provide recommended oversubscription factor and cache retention settings.

I'll need a quick confirmation on two items from Centurion: whether they can tolerate transient cold-start p99s during deploy windows and if they need dedicated HSM/KMS for key material.

-Karthik
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Liam — thanks for the fast turnaround and the sample. Marissa and I reviewed the preflight results Karthik sketched and attached a short summary (redwood-prelim-tiling-matrix.xlsx). Highlights:

- Recommended pilot: 24 GPUs split as 8 high-memory nodes for long-context sessions + 16 mixed-density for short/medium traffic.
- Expected typical p95 latency: 320 ms on lite routes, ~980 ms on long-form gen at pilot loads.
- Cost baseline (uncommitted hourly): estimated $0.78/token-equivalent for the tail; with a 3-month reserved pilot commit we can reduce unit cost ~22%.
- Suggested operational config: KV retention 8 minutes, session affinity enabled for streaming routes, canary routing for model-version rollout (10% traffic, 1-hour ramp).

Next steps:
- Liam: confirm HSM/KMS requirement and acceptance of the pilot commit duration (3 months).
- If yes, we'll prepare a Mutual Action Plan and a DocuSign for the reserved pilot.

Thanks — Kim

--
Kimberly Park
